summary: Yoshinobu Kimoto worked in Japanese history and archaeology. He studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, and held posts at Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993-2000), Koshien Junior College (president, 2000-2012), and Ryukoku University (professor, 2013-2021).
Yoshinobu Sakaide was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953-1957) under Mitsuji Fukunaga and held a post at Kansai University from around 1978 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1933-1946) under Hajime Tanabe, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1959-1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1976-1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944-1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1958-1961), and worked as an assistant in library affairs at Kyoto University from around 1949 to 1984.
Yoshio Takeuchi was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1907 to 1910 and held a post at Tohoku University from approximately 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani, EPHE, and Paris Diderot universities under Shoju Inaba, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Ariane Macdonald, and held posts at CNRS, Bhutan's National Library, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Toyo University, later holding posts at Toyo University, University of Tokyo (1972-1982), and Rissho University (~1980-1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University (1955-1977), and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1977-1987).
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. His career includes attested appointments at Kyoto University in 2006 and Kyoto National Museum in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman, among others, and served as professor and dean at Tenri University (~1984-2017).
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts as a researcher (attested 1998-2006) and specially appointed lecturer (attested 2015) at Taisho University.

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe studied at Tohoku University (D.Sc.) and served there as research associate (1975-2012) and senior research fellow (2018). He also founded the Asian Consortium on Computational Materials Science and held visiting appointments worldwide.
Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936-1939) and later served there as a professor from around 1950 to 1987.

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and held an associate professorship at Rowan University (attested 2003-2007).
Yu Yan Pang completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where they studied under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan, working in Buddhist studies.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued master's study at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, completed doctoral study under Natasha Heller (attested 2018), and studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Mou Zongsan and earned a PhD at McMaster University under Yün-hua Jan, later holding a post at National Central University (~1995-2004).
Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology scholar who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington and served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teacher Gongga Rinpoche and held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.
